registry.file: agent/runtime.ts:260-386 (buildRuntime, synchronous tool+capability registration); agent/runtime.ts:525-535 (attachMcp, async, called separately)
registry.note: buildRuntime() (agent/runtime.ts:104) builds a RegisteredTool[] array and a CapabilityId->CapabilityDecl Map at boot: fs x3 always via a single `...makeFsTools(scope)` spread (runtime.ts:299 - the three handlers live in agent/tools/fs.ts:324-375, not inline here), memory always, shell only if the sandbox probe succeeds, process x2 always, skill always, http always, search only if configured+keyed+allowlisted, capabilities Map assembled further down. Every real entrypoint (cli/repl.ts:111, cli/run.ts:30, cli/gateway.ts:297) then calls attachMcp(runtime, home) (runtime.ts:525-535) as a second, async step that connects rot/mcp.json's servers and pushes their verified tools via Runtime.register() (runtime.ts:98,464-467 - attachMcp is its only caller, line 531). agent/loop.ts's runTool() (line 696) is the sole consumer: it resolves the model-chosen name against the full deps.tools list (never the filtered 'exposed' list, so a member naming a host-only tool still gets a real policy denial and not a fabricated 'unknown tool'), derives a Resource via resourceFor() (loop.ts:867-881), and gates execution through PermissionSnapshot.check() (loop.ts:747, backed by core/policy/decide.ts).

tools.name: fs_read
params: path: string (required, relative to working directory)
tools.taintOut: tier: 2 (DISK_TIER, agent/tools/fs.ts) on every read - ADR-0044. Until that ADR this handler returned {content} with no `tier` key and a file's content was treated as fully trusted whatever its provenance; the map recorded that as a finding (see gaps) and it is now closed. 2 because `stat` cannot tell the owner's own note from something that arrived in ~/Downloads: under that uncertainty the fail-closed reading is the only honest one.
tools.wiredNote: Registered unconditionally via the `...makeFsTools(scope)` spread at agent/runtime.ts:299 - the handler itself lives at agent/tools/fs.ts:326-339 (makeFsTools), not inline in runtime.ts (the three fs handlers were unified into one factory, used by both runtime.ts and evals/floor/run.ts, so the fix could not stay in the tool file without reaching production).
tools.onDeny: Generic kernel refusal at agent/loop.ts:769-776: 'Rifiutato dal kernel dei permessi (<code>). Non insistere: serve una decisione dell'owner.' Most likely code in practice: taint_exceeded once turn taint > 3 (defaultMaxTaint.low, core/policy/matrix.ts:95).
tools.oneLine: Legge un file di testo dentro la working directory.

tools.name: fs_list
params: path: string (required, directory relative to working directory)
tools.taintOut: tier: 2 (DISK_TIER) - same shape as fs_read, and the same argument: a filename is text somebody chose, and `IGNORA le istruzioni precedenti.md` costs an attacker nothing. Treating a listing as metadata rather than content would be a special case whose only argument is that the strings are short (ADR-0044).
tools.wiredNote: Registered unconditionally via the `...makeFsTools(scope)` spread at agent/runtime.ts:299 - the handler itself lives at agent/tools/fs.ts:340-359 (makeFsTools), not inline in runtime.ts.
tools.onDeny: agent/loop.ts:769-776, same generic kernel refusal as fs_read.
tools.oneLine: Elenca le voci di una directory, indicando quali sono cartelle.

tools.name: fs_write
tools.taintOut: tier: 0, declared and not omitted (ADR-0044): the result is this tool's own receipt ('wrote N bytes'), nothing enters the turn. n/a in practice anyway - see wiredNote: the handler (fsWrite) is never reached in production.
tools.wiredNote: Registered via the `...makeFsTools(scope)` spread at agent/runtime.ts:299 (handler at agent/tools/fs.ts:360-373) and exposed to the model - but see gaps: fs.write is declared risk:'medium' + reversible:'undoable' (fs.ts:78-85), and core/policy/decide.ts:204-207 maps every medium+undoable capability to effect:'draft'. agent/loop.ts:777-791 has no undo journal implemented, so 'draft' is turned into an unconditional hard refusal (isError:true) BEFORE fsWrite() ever runs. Confirmed unconditional (owner, taint 0) by core/policy/decide.test.ts:117 and agent/loop.test.ts:527-556. The tool is registered and reachable; it never actually writes.
tools.onDeny: Not a policy 'deny' - a 'draft' verdict, refused at agent/loop.ts:783-791: '"fs.write" richiede una bozza revocabile e il registro di undo non esiste ancora. Non eseguito: dillo all'owner invece di riprovare.'
tools.oneLine: Scriverebbe un file, ma il verdetto 'draft' lo blocca sempre.

tools.name: memory_search
tools.taintOut: Dynamic: the max trustTier across the recalled items, 0 if none (agent/tools/memory.ts:90-93). Same rule the pre-loop's own recall applies, deliberately, per the file's docstring.
tools.wiredNote: Registered unconditionally at agent/runtime.ts:279-289. Tenant is bound from ToolContext at call time (handler: (args, ctx) => searchMemory(recallDeps, ctx.tenant, args), runtime.ts:284), not from the tool's own arguments - see gaps re: its resourceKind:'tenant' declaration.
tools.onDeny: agent/loop.ts:769-776 generic refusal; hostOnly:false (memory.ts:29-30) so group members are NOT blocked by principal_forbidden, unlike every host-only tool.
tools.oneLine: Cerca nella memoria del tenant: conversazioni, documenti, fatti appresi.

tools.name: shell_run
params: cwd?: string (relative to project root, default root)
tools.taintOut: tier: 2 - formatExecOutcome (agent/tools/shell.ts) returns DISK_TIER, the same constant fs_read uses, because `cat ~/Downloads/nota.md` is fs_read through another door and a door that did not taint was a way around the one that did (ADR-0044). maxTaint: 2, not the inherited defaultMaxTaint.high = 1 - owner decision, 2026-08-16 (ADR-0044, Revisione 2026-08-16): at taint 2 sys.shell is ask (one read downgrades the hardened auto-allow to a prompt instead of ending shell access outright); at taint 3 - a web/search/mcp result - it is still deny/taint_exceeded. The ceiling moved by one step, not away.
tools.wiredNote: Conditionally registered at agent/runtime.ts:301-304: only if `new SandboxExecutor(guards).status().available` is true, i.e. core/sandbox/executor.ts:75-78's probeSandbox() found a real OS-level containment on this host. Absent sandbox -> absent tool entirely, never an unsandboxed fallback (ADR-0018 rule 5, per the file's own docstring lines 27-30).
tools.onDeny: High risk: core/policy/decide.ts:208-213 allows only if hardened && owner principal && taint===0; otherwise ask(`sys.shell on ...`). If an approver is wired (agent/loop.ts:792-816), the owner is prompted and a 'no' returns 'L'owner ha rifiutato ... Non insistere' (loop.ts:806-813). If no approver is wired (see gaps), the turn stops early with stopped:'ask' and a pending ApprovalRequest (loop.ts:112-117, 577-590) instead of a normal tool_result.
tools.oneLine: Esegue un comando shell non interattivo, sandboxato, senza rete.

tools.name: process_list
params: grep?: string (case-insensitive substring filter, max 200 chars)
tools.taintOut: tier: 1 (ADR-0044) - the host's own process table, and `PS_ARGV` asks for `comm`, never `args`. Not DISK_TIER: choosing one of those strings costs an attacker code execution on the host, while planting a file in ~/Downloads costs them an email. Deliberately at (not above) the maxTaint:1 this capability pins, so listing processes does not become a once-per-turn tool.
tools.wiredNote: Registered unconditionally at agent/runtime.ts:310 via makeProcessTools() (both process tools come from one call).
tools.onDeny: agent/loop.ts:769-776 generic; realistically taint_exceeded once turn taint > 1 - a tight, explicit ceiling (process.ts:27) narrower than the low-risk default of 3, so this tool goes unreachable after a single tier-2+ event (e.g. one memory recall of group-authored content).
tools.oneLine: Elenca i processi in corso sull'host (pid, utente, comando).

tools.name: process_kill
tools.taintOut: tier: 0 on every path (ADR-0044): a kill is a write, and every string it can return - a refusal, a translated errno, the delivery receipt - is one this file wrote. Nothing enters the turn.
tools.wiredNote: Registered unconditionally at agent/runtime.ts:310 via makeProcessTools() (same call as process_list).
tools.onDeny: Same high-risk ask/refuse pattern as shell_run (core/policy/decide.ts:208-213); same approve-wiring gap applies (see gaps). Schema itself rejects pid<=1 and the agent's own pid is refused in the handler (process.ts:146-148: 'refused: <pid> is the agent process itself').
tools.oneLine: Invia un segnale (default TERM) a un processo dato il pid.

tools.name: skill_read
params: file?: string (path relative to the skill dir, max 500 chars)
tools.taintOut: tier: 1, always (skill.ts:127) - deliberately not tier 0 and not fenced. The file's own comment (skill.ts:114-121) documents a since-fixed defect: an omitted tier let a skill body reach context at taint 0, which combined with decide.ts's hardened-high-risk branch (taint===0 required for a silent allow) meant a turn could read a skill's instructions and then reach sys.shell without the owner ever being asked. Current code sets tier:1 and this file's docstring calls skill bodies 'instructions on purpose' (owner-installed, owner-audited).
tools.wiredNote: Registered unconditionally at agent/runtime.ts:346, over whatever discoverSkills(home) found at boot (skillScan.skills); parse failures are reported as boot lines (runtime.ts:488), never silently dropped.
tools.oneLine: Legge SKILL.md o un file allegato di una skill installata.

tools.name: http_get
tools.taintOut: 3 on every real HTTP response, 2xx through non-2xx alike (fenced via core/memory/spotlight.js fence()), including after local main-content extraction (agent/tools/extract.ts) when the body is text/html or application/xhtml+xml. Transport/validation failures (bad URL, DNS SSRF veto, blocked redirect, fetch exception, unparseable redirect location) return `tier: 0` - explicitly since ADR-0044, where they used to carry no `tier` key and meant the same thing only by accident.
tools.onDeny: medium+reversible:'yes' -> core/policy/decide.ts:204-207 allow (never drafts). Two extra kernel branches specific to url-resourceKind capabilities: the allowlist check at decide.ts:155-193 (off-allowlist -> ask for the owner only if taint<=1, else deny/resource_denied) PLUS the tool's own re-check of every redirect hop against the same allowlist (http.ts:97-104), because the kernel only ever saw hop 0's host.
tools.oneLine: Scarica un URL via GET, solo host in allowlist.

tools.name: web_search
tools.taintOut: 3 on a successful search including zero-hit responses ('nessun risultato ...'), fenced. `tier: 0` when the backend call itself throws - 'nothing from the provider reached us, so there is nothing to be tainted by', now stated rather than left unstated (ADR-0044).
tools.wiredNote: Conditionally registered at agent/runtime.ts:333-370: only if config.search is set AND the Tavily API key resolves (readSecret) AND api.tavily.com passes hostAllowed() against rot/egress.json, checked ONCE at boot (search.ts:33-41 explains why: the endpoint is a constant, so gating it per-call would be a no-op). Any failure degrades to a boot-line note (runtime.ts:349-351, 365-368) and the tool is simply absent, not broken.
tools.onDeny: hostOnly:true (search.ts:55) so a group member is refused principal_forbidden before risk logic even runs (core/policy/decide.ts:128-130) - unlike http_get, which a member CAN reach. Otherwise medium+reversible:'yes' allows like http_get.
tools.oneLine: Cerca sul web: restituisce titoli, URL e brevi estratti.

tools.name: mcp_<server>_<tool>
tools.file: agent/tools/mcp.ts:93-114 (built per remote tool, inside buildMcpTools' loop starting at mcp.ts:61)
params: dynamic - def.inputSchema taken verbatim from the remote MCP server's tool definition and passed through opaquely (mcp.ts:102 comment: 'the shape is the server's contract and the provider passes it through opaquely'), hash-verified against the owner's pin before being trusted
tools.taintOut: 3 always, on both success AND error results alike (mcp.ts:106-111: `tier: 3, ...(result.isError?{isError:true}:{})` are set unconditionally) - unlike http_get/web_search, even a remote tool's own error message taints the turn exactly like a success would.
tools.wiredNote: NOT registered inside buildRuntime()/the synchronous tools array. Registered by attachMcp() (agent/runtime.ts:525-535), a separate async function called after buildRuntime() by every real surface - cli/repl.ts:133, cli/run.ts:47, cli/gateway.ts:363 - which loads rot/mcp.json's registry, connects each server, and for each one that VERIFIES (live tool defs hash-match the owner's pin, mcp.ts:71-88) pushes its tools via Runtime.register() (runtime.ts:464-467, called at runtime.ts:531). A server whose tools don't match its pin is SUSPENDED: zero tools, zero capability, one Italian report line naming what changed (mcp.ts:74-88), and re-approval via `muffin mcp add <server>` is the only way back. Zero MCP capabilities/tools exist until rot/mcp.json lists at least one server.
tools.onDeny: hostOnly:true (mcp.ts:37) so a group member is refused principal_forbidden before risk logic runs. Otherwise medium+reversible:'no' -> core/policy/decide.ts:204-207 allow (never drafts, unlike fs.write). Ceiling is DELIBERATELY inherited (maxTaint omitted) rather than pinned, per mcp.ts:20-28's own warning: pinning is the fallback ONLY if the matrix's downward-clamp (core/policy/matrix.ts `tighter()`) is ever removed.
tools.oneLine: Chiama un tool di un server MCP remoto, verificato.

capabilities.note: 1:1 with fs_read. No maxTaint declared -> inherits defaultMaxTaint.low = 3 (core/policy/matrix.ts:95), deliberately not pinned so an owner who lowers policy.json's low ceiling is obeyed (fs.ts:34-61 argues this at length: the alternative would break search-then-read-notes in one turn).
1:1 with fs_list. Same inherited ceiling as fs.read.

1:1 with fs_write - but see gaps. reversible:'undoable' routes every call to the kernel's 'draft' verdict (core/policy/decide.ts:204-207), and agent/loop.ts always hard-refuses 'draft' because no undo journal exists (loop.ts:777-791). The capability, the tool and the registration all exist and are reachable; only the write itself never happens, for anyone, at any taint.

1:1 with memory_search. Declares resourceKind:'tenant' + policyArgs:['query'] (memory.ts:25-26), but see gaps: agent/loop.ts's resourceFor() (loop.ts:867-881) only ever constructs 'url' or 'path' resources, never 'tenant' - this declaration never reaches decide() as a real Resource. Tenant scoping is real but happens structurally instead, via ToolContext.tenant threaded straight to the handler (loop.ts:824, memory.ts:48-52).

1:1 with process_list. Ceiling explicitly pinned to 1, narrower than the low-risk default of 3 - process.ts:18-20 states why: 'the matrix row for host processes denies everything at taint >=2, so the list capability narrows its ceiling explicitly.'
1:1 with process_kill. No maxTaint declared, but high's default ceiling is already 1 (matrix.ts:95), so nothing would change by pinning it.

1:1 with shell_run, but the tool is registered only when the sandbox probe succeeds (agent/runtime.ts:301-304) - an install without a working sandbox has a declared capability with no tool behind it at all.
1:1 with http_get. Ceiling explicitly widened to 3 above the medium default of 1, reasoned about at length in decide.ts:32-43 (a tainted turn may still read another public page).

1:1 with web_search, but the tool is registered only when config.search + a resolvable API key + an egress-allowlisted endpoint all hold (agent/runtime.ts:333-370) - otherwise the capability is simply never added to the map at all (runtime.ts:384: '...(searchOn ? [searchCapability] : [])'), so this is one of the few capability declarations that is itself conditional, not just its tool.

1:1 with skill_read. Ceiling pinned to 1 - narrower than low's default of 3 - specifically so a tainted turn cannot read a skill body and then combine it with the hardened-mode shell auto-allow (see skill_read's taintOut for the historical near-miss this closed).

capabilities.file: agent/tools/mcp.ts:30-39 (mcpCapabilityFor - a template function, not a static constant)
capabilities.note: One instance PER connected+hash-verified MCP server, not a single static id - created by mcpCapabilityFor(server) inside buildMcpTools' loop (mcp.ts:91) and registered late via attachMcp()/Runtime.register(), never inside buildRuntime() itself. Zero instances exist until rot/mcp.json lists a server; a server whose live tool defs don't hash-match its pin gets zero tools AND zero capability ('SOSPESO', mcp.ts:74-88). maxTaint is deliberately left undeclared (inherits medium's default of 1) - mcp.ts:20-28 warns this must stay inherited, not pinned, unless core/policy/matrix.ts's downward-only clamp on policy.json is ever removed; a judge run once measured that exact clamp's absence turning this into a silent allow at taint 3.

gaps.what: fs_write is fully registered, declared, schema-valid and reachable by the model - and can never actually write a file. fs.write is declared risk:'medium' + reversible:'undoable' (agent/tools/fs.ts:78-85). core/policy/decide.ts:204-207 maps EVERY medium+undoable capability to effect:'draft'. agent/loop.ts:777-791 has no undo journal implemented, so the 'draft' case is an unconditional hard refusal (isError:true, 'il registro di undo non esiste ancora') - the fsWrite() function itself (fs.ts:257-262) is fully correct code with no caller in production.
gaps.evidence: agent/tools/fs.ts:78-85; core/policy/decide.ts:204-207; agent/loop.ts:777-791; confirmed by tests at core/policy/decide.test.ts:117 (draft even for owner at taint 0) and agent/loop.test.ts:527-556 ('refuses a draft instead of executing it as an allow')
gaps.why_it_matters: The only declared write capability among 'the three filesystem primitives of M1' (fs.ts:7) is inert in every build that ships today - an owner asking Muffin to save a note or edit a file gets the same fixed Italian refusal every single time, and no runtime configuration changes that outcome; only building the undo journal would.

gaps.what: The owner-approval channel (LoopDeps.approve) is implemented on exactly one of the three real surfaces. cli/repl.ts:157-164 sets runtime.deps.approve (reads a yes/no from the terminal's stdin). cli/gateway.ts - the headless daemon that hosts the Telegram connector via cli/surface.ts:187-267 (connectSurfaces, called identically by both repl.ts and gateway.ts) - never sets it anywhere in the file. cli/surface.ts:209-210 builds TelegramConnector with `loop: runtime.deps` as-is, no override.
gaps.evidence: agent/loop.ts:172 (Approver is optional on LoopDeps); agent/loop.ts:798-803 (no approver -> throw ApprovalRequired, turning into stopped:'ask' at loop.ts:577-590 with the text 'Su questa superficie non posso chiederla.'); cli/repl.ts:157-164 (the only .approve assignment found in cli/ or agent/, via grep); cli/gateway.ts (zero occurrences of 'approve'); connectors/telegram/connector.ts:307-317 (runs the turn, forwards only result.text to the chat, never reads result.pending)
gaps.why_it_matters: cli/run.ts:96-113 treats a missing approval channel as a deliberate, documented design for a one-shot script ('Headless has no channel by design', exits 3 and tells the operator to relaunch interactively) - but cli/gateway.ts is not a script, it is the always-on daemon meant to host Telegram for ongoing use. On that surface sys.shell and sys.process.kill are permanently un-approvable for the owner too, not just group members: there is no code path today that can turn their 'ask' verdict into an 'allow' outside a foreground `muffin` terminal session, and the turn only ever reports this politely in the chat rather than at boot.

gaps.what: CLOSED by ADR-0044 (2026-08-15). WAS: five of the ten static tool handlers never set ToolOutcome.tier at all - fs_read, fs_list, shell_run (formatExecOutcome), process_list and process_kill all returned a plain {content}, and agent/loop.ts raised taint only when outcome.tier was present, so none of the five could ever raise the turn's taint. NOW: `tier` is a REQUIRED field on ToolOutcome, so the omission is a compile error rather than a silent zero, and the loop raises unconditionally. fs_read/fs_list/shell_run carry DISK_TIER = 2, process_list carries 1, process_kill and the pure-error paths carry an explicit 0.
gaps.evidence: docs/blueprint/adr/0044-il-disco-non-ha-provenienza.md; agent/loop.ts (`tier: TrustTier` required, `snapshot.raiseTaint(outcome.tier)` unconditional); agent/tools/fs.ts (DISK_TIER, makeFsTools); agent/read-then-egress.test.ts (the chain, measured red first); agent/runtime-wiring.test.ts (the same chain through buildRuntime)
gaps.why_it_matters: This map found it and could not tell whether it was a decision or an omission - and it was worse than either: fs.ts's own long comment argued its high taint ceiling by leaning on the egress gate ('off-allowlist above taint 1 is DENY, never ask'), and that gate reads the turn's taint, which the read did not raise. The security argument written in the file depended on a property the file did not produce. Measured before the fix: fs_read of an injected file, then http_get to an off-allowlist host, came back as an `ask` the owner approved and the fetch ran. The cost of the fix is stated and deliberate: a turn that has read from disk can no longer act on the host (shell, skill_read, process, mcp all become taint_exceeded), which is threat model 03 section 3's own row applied to a context that swallowed unprovenanced bytes.

gaps.what: memory.read declares resourceKind:'tenant' and policyArgs:['query'] (agent/tools/memory.ts:25-26), and the Resource type has a matching {kind:'tenant', value: TenantId} variant (core/policy/types.ts:40-44) - but agent/loop.ts's resourceFor(), the only function that turns a capability declaration plus call args into a kernel-facing Resource, exclusively special-cases 'url' and 'path' and returns {kind:'none'} for anything else (loop.ts:867-881). No 'tenant' Resource is ever constructed by any code path read in this repo.
gaps.why_it_matters: Reading the declaration alone, it looks like the kernel checks the tenant resource per call the way it checks 'url' against the egress allowlist (decide.ts:155-193) - it does not; core/policy/decide.ts has no branch on resource.kind==='tenant' at all. Real tenant scoping for memory_search does hold, but entirely outside decide(), via ToolContext.tenant threaded straight into the handler (loop.ts:824, memory.ts:48-52) - which is safe today only because that wiring is correct, not because the declared resourceKind is doing any enforcement.
